cli.help.action.identity: Resolve a copied or restored installation identity
cli.help.identity:
Usage: deckent init identity --keep|--new [--json] [--lang en|tr]
--keep: Same installation (move/restore): keep identity and update binding.
--new: New installation: generate a new installationId; preserve projects.
Only an explicit choice updates the local identity record.
cli.help.run:
Usage: deckent run <action>
People start work with deckent do --request <text> and find it with deckent run list. Every action takes a short id (a unique prefix, as in git).
  list [--scope <id>] [--limit <n>] [--json] [--lang en|tr]
  inspect [--scope <id>] [--id <run>] [--verbose] [--json] [--lang en|tr]
  cancel|hold|resume|close [--scope <id>] [--id <run>] [--reason <text>]
On a terminal without --id the Run is picked, its revision is read for you and a card names the scope and the Run before anything is sent.
AI and automation keep every typed flag:
  cancel|close --scope <id> --id <run> --command-id <id> --expected-revision <n>
  hold --scope <id> --id <run> --command-id <id> --expected-revision <n> --reason <text>
  resume --scope <id> --id <run> --command-id <id> --expected-revision <n> [--task <id> --answer <text>] [--quota wait|next-candidate]
  create --scope <id> --id <run> --command-id <id> --graph <file|-> [--branch <file>] [--delivery-command-id <id>]
  reserve --scope <id> --id <run> --command-id <id> --expected-revision <n>
  propose --proposal <file|-> [--json] [--lang en|tr]
  inspect-proposal --scope <id> --id <run> --command-id <id> [--json] [--lang en|tr]
create, propose and reserve take typed JSON for AI and automation; a person uses deckent do. Run creation admits a graph; reservation selects Tasks and generates Attempt identities. Neither executes Tasks or accepts a caller verdict.
--graph - reads graph JSON from piped stdin. The standard Run path uses the local service: deckent runtime serve.
cli.help.task:
Usage: deckent task <action>
  inspect --scope <id> --run <id> --task <id> [--json] [--lang en|tr]
  execute --scope <id> --run <id> --task <id> --attempt <id> --generation <n>
    --layout-revision <id> [--json] [--lang en|tr] [--no-color]
  evaluate --scope <id> --run <id> --task <id> --attempt <id> --generation <n>
    --layout-revision <id> --command-id <id> --expected-revision <n> [--json]
    [--lang en|tr] [--no-color]
  accept|reject --scope <id> --run <run> --task <task> --command-id <id>
    --expected-revision <n> [--json] [--lang en|tr] [--no-color]
Execution records terminal process evidence; evaluation decides Task acceptance
    from recorded evidence. A terminal result alone is not acceptance.
  task patch-prepare|patch-preview --scope <id> --run <id> --task <id>
    --attempt <id> --generation <n> --layout-revision <id> [--json]
    patch-preview: [--stat|--diff] (diff is the default; not with --json)
  task integration-check|integration-prepare --scope <id> --run <id>
    --task <id> --attempt <id> --generation <n> --layout-revision <id>
    [--json] [--lang en|tr]
  integration-prepare: --command-id <id> --proposal <code>
  integration-prepare: [--replaces-command-id <id>]
  task integration-inspect --scope <id> --run <id> --task <id>
    --attempt <id> --generation <n> --layout-revision <id>
    --command-id <id> [--json]
  patch-preview, transcript, integration-inspect: --attempt,
    --generation and --layout-revision may all be omitted; the latest
    attempt of --run/--task is used (partial sets are a usage error)
  task integration-deliver --scope <id> --run <id> --task <id>
    --attempt <id> --generation <n> --layout-revision <id>
    --command-id <id> --candidate-command-id <id> [--json]
  task integration-adopt --scope <id> --run <id> --task <id> --attempt <id>
    --generation <n> --layout-revision <id> --command-id <id>
    --delivery-command-id <id> --target refs/heads/<branch>
    [--verification-run <run>] [--json]
  task integration-rollback --scope <id> --run <id> --task <id>
    --attempt <id> --generation <n> --layout-revision <id>
    --command-id <id> --adoption-command-id <id>
Adoption moves a configured branch that no worktree has checked out; it is
    verified only with --verification-run (kind from
    execution.adoption.verification).
  task transcript --scope <id> --run <id> --task <id> --attempt <id>
    --generation <n> --layout-revision <id> [--json]
Execution and evaluation use the local service: deckent runtime serve.
Patch preparation and preview use local policy/storage without that service.
cli.help.pool:
Usage: deckent pool [<action>]
  (no action) | status [--scope <id>] [--pool <id>] [--json]   the pool in human words (reads the configured scope and says so)
  hold | resume [--scope <id>] [--pool <id>] [--reason <text>] [--json]
  set-capacity --execution-slots <n> --in-flight-slots <n> [--scope <id>] [--pool <id>] [--json]
  quota-release --channel <id> [--scope <id>] [--pool <id>] [--json]
A change never takes a silent scope: off a terminal --scope is required (exit 2 otherwise, nothing written); on a terminal you pick the scope and confirm what changes, on which pool and why; capacity values come from preset options there.
While a pool is held no new task is reserved; running work finishes and is evaluated; stop running work with deckent run cancel. hold/resume need installation-level authority (pool hold|resume over all scopes); quota-release needs its own pool release-quota authority. --pool defaults to the admission pool.

cli.help.runtime:
Usage: deckent runtime [<action>]
  (no action) | describe [--json]   status: running or not, build, configuration current, running work, socket
  shutdown [--reason <text>] [--force] [--json]   governed stop built from the live service (off a terminal --reason is required; a service a manager such as systemd runs is refused unless --force: stop it through its manager)
  shutdown --service <id> --instance <id> --command-id <id> --reason <text> [--json]
  restart [--json]   stop, then start from the current build and configuration
  serve [--json]   run the service in the foreground
The service normally starts by itself when you open deckent; serve is for running it by hand. On a terminal shutdown and restart show the running work they affect on a card first; stopping never cancels worker operations.

cli.help.models:
Usage: deckent models [--scope <id>] [--declared] [--catalog] [--verbose] [--json] [--lang en|tr]
Two lists: declared = what the connected providers declare (the terminal's chat models) · catalog = the models workers may use.
Without an action: one table of the catalog models of the scope (configured scope when omitted), grouped by channel: model, channel
(subscription / API / local), state (active, inactive, retired with its day), effort. A switched-on model retiring within
models.retirementWarningDays (default 15) is warned about. --declared shows the declared list; --verbose adds revisions and catalog facts.
--json alone prints the declared list (unchanged contract); --catalog --json (or --scope <id> --json) prints the catalog table's data.
  models activate|deactivate        on a terminal: provider, exact model id, then a scoped card
  models connect                    on a terminal: connection, exact model id, then a scoped card
  models catalog activate|deactivate  on a terminal: channel, model, then a scoped card
  models roles [set]                which model serves which role (new model: role pending); set: a card on a terminal
  models spending                   the scope's API budget: limit, used, held, left
  models binding|activation|activate|deactivate --help
  models invoke|invocation|purge-content|spending|audit-spending --input <file|-> [--json]
Invoke, invocation, purge-content, spending --input and audit-spending require an explicitly started local `deckent runtime serve`. A runtime-owned invocation continues if the client disconnects; retrying the same command identity returns its receipt and does not resend the native request.
  models catalog --help
cli.help.modelsBinding:
Usage: deckent models binding --provider <id> --provider-version <version> --model <id> --model-version <version> [--json] [--lang <locale>] [--no-color]
Inspect the exact declared native model definition and its SHA-256 content binding. This does not activate a model or authorize execution.
cli.help.modelsCatalog:
Usage: deckent models catalog list --scope <id> [--channel <id>] [--json] [--lang <locale>]
       deckent models catalog register --scope <id> --command-id <id> (--seed <name> | --file <file|->) [--json]
       deckent models catalog activate|deactivate --scope <id> --channel <id> [--model <exact_id>] --command-id <id> --expected-revision <n> [--json]
The ledger model catalog for worker Runs: channels and exact model ids with lifecycle, CLI minimum and per-scope activation. register writes installation-wide facts and needs a model-activation grant over all scopes; activate/deactivate change one scope. --seed reads a packaged document: claude-cli-subscription, codex-cli-subscription or cursor-cli-subscription. Replaying a command id returns its receipt.
       deckent models catalog activate|deactivate [--scope <id>] [--channel <id>]
On a terminal, without --command-id and --expected-revision, this asks the channel and the model; the expected revision is read by the system, then a scoped card confirms.
cli.help.modelsActivation:
Usage: deckent models activation|activate|deactivate --scope <id> --provider <id> --provider-version <version> --model <id> --model-version <version> [--json] [--lang <locale>] [--no-color]
activate/deactivate also require --command-id <id> --expected-revision <n> --binding-digest SHA256. activate additionally requires --catalog-revision REV.
Inspect recorded state or submit an explicit activation command. This does not establish provider availability or invocation permission.
On a terminal, `deckent models activate|deactivate [--scope <id>]` asks the provider and the exact model id; the binding digest and revisions are read by the system, then a scoped card confirms.
cli.help.modelsInvocation:
deckent models invoke|invocation --input <file|-> [--json] [--lang en|tr]
invoke: native command JSON; invocation: persisted receipt query JSON. Both require an explicitly started local `deckent runtime serve`. A runtime-owned invocation continues if the client disconnects; retrying the same command identity returns its receipt and does not resend the native request.
cli.help.modelsPurgeContent:
deckent models purge-content --input <file|-> [--json] [--lang en|tr]
Purges active retained native, usage, or raw response content after separate purge-content policy authorization. It preserves the invocation outcome, quota record, and no-resend identity.
cli.help.modelsCancelInvocation:
deckent models cancel --input <file|-> [--json] [--lang en|tr]
Records a cancellation request by exact invocation command identity. It can prevent dispatch before send permission; after permission it does not prove remote cancellation or completion.
cli.help.modelsSpending:
deckent models spending [--scope <id>] [--json] [--lang en|tr]
  Without --input: the scope's API budget in money (limit, used, held for running calls, left); the configured scope when omitted.
deckent models spending --input <file|-> [--json] [--lang en|tr]
Read the exact scoped provider-spending account snapshot from the explicitly started local `deckent runtime serve`. Input is schema 1: scopeId, budgetId, and budgetRevision. Reserved amounts include held reservations, but this view does not show hold reasons. The settled total may combine local calculations and provider-reported charges; source subtotals are not included. This is local recorded accounting evidence, not a provider invoice or an audited spending history.
cli.help.modelsAuditSpending:
deckent models audit-spending --input <file|-> [--json] [--lang en|tr]
Record a bounded integrity audit for one exact provider-spending checkpoint through the explicitly started local `deckent runtime serve`. Input is schema 1: commandId, scopeId, budgetId, budgetRevision, and expectedCheckpointDigest. It records an immutable audit receipt; it does not correct financial records, verify an invoice, or prove a complete invocation audit.
cli.help.inference:
deckent inference [--profile <id>] [--json] [--lang en|tr]   status: the active serving profile, or what is missing
  inference plan [--profile <id>] [--json] [--lang en|tr]
  inference budget [--profile <id>] [--reserve-id <id> --reserve-role brain|worker|auditor --reserve-tokens <n>] [--json]
  inference metrics [--profile <id>] [--json] [--lang en|tr]
A serving profile (inference_serving) describes a vLLM server you run: it derives the launch arguments and a capacity estimate. A local model connected as a provider (deckent models) is a different thing: it is how Deckent calls that server. metrics reads a loopback /metrics URL using that profile's metrics limits and does not start the server.
cli.help.terminal:
deckent [terminal] [--scope <id>] [--full-access]   interactive terminal (same
  as `terminal workline`)
  terminal status [--json] [--lang en|tr]
  terminal chat-plan [--lang en|tr]
  terminal snapshot [--lang en|tr]
  terminal session [--scope <id>] [--lang en|tr]
  terminal workline [--scope <id>] [--lang en|tr] [--no-color] [--full-access]
Chat turns are governed model invocations through the local runtime service
  (`deckent runtime serve`) for the model named in `terminal.chat`. session is
  line mode and also reads piped input; workline needs an interactive terminal
  on stdin and stdout.

The scope defaults to `terminal.scopeId`. When no runtime service is running,
  the terminal starts one in the background; it keeps running after exit
  (`deckent runtime shutdown`).

--full-access opens the session in full access (tool calls run without asking;
  Deckent's own state, policy and credentials stay closed); it needs a company
  grant. Inside a session, Shift+Tab or `/mode full-access` switches into it for
  that session only (nothing is stored); every later turn is checked on the
  grant again.
  terminal session --trust-instructions <sha256>

cli.help.policy:
Usage: deckent policy [status] [--scope <id>] [--verbose] [--json]
  Summary: kind, administrators, my grants, AI steps and MCP groups.
  deckent policy grants [--scope <id>] [--json]
    My standing approvals (--mine kept).
  deckent policy grants --all [--after <mark>] [--scope <id>] [--json]
    Everyone's standing approvals, one page; needs policy inspect-standing-grants.
  deckent policy scopes [--json]
  deckent policy vocabulary [--json]
    A table; the raw matrix with --json.
  deckent policy revoke <id> [--scope <id>] [--yes] [--json]
  deckent policy upgrade --template current [--scope <id>]
    [--preview|--apply|--rollback] [--expect <revision>] [--json]
  deckent policy mcp [--scope <id>]
    On your terminal: pick a group, preview, apply; elsewhere the list.
  deckent policy mcp list [--scope <id>] [--json]
  deckent policy mcp grant|revoke|narrow --group <id> --scope <id>
    [--preview|--apply --expect <digest>] [--json]
    narrow: an earlier, wider grant shrinks to the group's current version.
  deckent policy delegations [--scope <id>] [--resource <id>] [--json]
    On your terminal: pick a step, preview, apply.
  deckent policy delegate|undelegate --scope <id> --step <step>
    [--actor mcp] [--resource <id>] [--json]
cli.help.mcp:
Usage: deckent mcp [<action>]
  (no action) | list [--check]
    One table: name, scope, state, connection, command or URL; waiting servers first with their next step.
    Nothing starts; --check starts trusted servers only and shows their connection.
    On a terminal, bare `deckent mcp` then lets you pick a server and approve, revoke or remove it.
  add [--scope local|project|user] [--transport stdio] [--env <KEY=value>]
    [--realm <realm>] [--timeout-ms <n>] [--no-approve] <name> -- <command> [args]
  add [--scope …] [--transport http] [--header '<Name: value>'] <name> <url>
  add                            on a terminal: a form (name, type, command or URL, scope), a preview card, then its trust cards
  add-json [--scope local|project|user] [--no-approve] <name> <json>
  import [--from claude-code|claude-desktop|<file>] [--scope local|user]   on a terminal without --from: pick the client
  get <name>
  remove [<name>] [--scope local|project|user]
  approve [<name>] [--always-ask <tool>] [--no-always-ask]
  revoke [<name>]
Trusting a server (approve; add to a local or user scope) is a person's card on a terminal: off a terminal it is refused,
and --yes no longer skips the card. Without a name on a terminal, approve, revoke and remove let you pick the server.
A header or env value may name a secret as $DECK:NAME (local, user scope).
Imported servers are not trusted: each asks for approval before it starts.
cli.help.secret:
Usage: deckent secret [<action>]
  (no action) | list [--all] [--scope <id>] [--json]   name · vault · project · used by · .deck · grant · stored; never a value
    --all: every project vault of this main vault (names only; the key store administrator)
  set [<name>] --main|--project [--scope <id>]   value only at the hidden prompt of your terminal (a piped value is refused before it is read), never an argument; on a terminal without --main/--project a card asks which vault, with --json it is refused (SECRET_VAULT_REQUIRED); on a terminal without a name pick a key the config references but the store lacks
  delete <name> [--main|--project] [--scope <id>]   on a terminal a card shows who still uses it
  grant <name> --scope <id>   let this project use a main-vault key (a card at your own terminal; AI sessions cannot); revoke <name> --scope <id> takes it back
  handover --scope <id>   a moved project takes its key vault along (refused while the original folder still holds it)
  store [--to <store>] [--confirm-downgrade] [--confirm-env-missing] [--list] [--scope <id>]
    without --to off a terminal: the current store and the options explained (env = environment variables, file = plain file, less safe, encrypted-file = encrypted, its key in the same folder); on a terminal: picker, and a separate warning card before a weaker store
A project uses a main key only with a grant; its own keys (set --project) only when .deck declares NAME=project.
A change never takes a silent scope: off a terminal --scope is required.
cli.help.toolchains:
Usage: deckent toolchains [update [--apply]] [--json]
  (no action)   tool · accepted · newest · state (checks the package registry over the network, said first) and whether updates run by themselves
  update   plan the next worker image; off a terminal it only reports
  update --apply   build it (Docker image, up to toolchains.update.buildTimeoutMs, 30 min by default); writes a profile proposal and changes no profile
On a terminal the plan is shown on a card and only Apply builds. Running work keeps its current image. Health check only: deckent doctor --toolchains.
cli.help.doctor:
Usage: deckent doctor [--verbose] [--toolchains] [--json]
Check the installation without starting work. Rows are grouped (Installation, Security, Work, Tools), each with ok / warning /
error / not tested and, for a problem, the one next step.
--verbose   also print the details (paths, store ids, realm notices)
--toolchains also ask the npm registry for the newest worker CLIs (uses the network; read-only)
--json      print the full report for scripts and AI tools
On your own terminal, a fixable row is offered as a card (apply / not now) and applied only through the product's own command;
a pipe, script or AI caller is never asked.
cli.help.inventory:
Usage: deckent inventory [--scope <id>] [--after <id>] [--limit <n>] [--verbose] [--json]
Developer view: this installation's stored execution records (one per attempt), in bounded pages. Without --scope: the configured default scope.
People follow work with deckent run list. deckent workers list also reads the other worker sources configured for the scope, so it can show more records than this view.
cli.help.paths:
Usage: deckent paths [--global] [--json]
The installation's paths grouped (configuration, records and data, security, runtime, terminal) with exists/missing, then this user's files (global folder, MCP definitions, secret store file). The runtime socket really used is a short /tmp path (Unix socket paths hold at most 108 bytes). --global: only the global installation. --json keeps the layout inspection document.

cli.coding.template.help:
deckent coding template [--provider <id>] [--kind <kind>] [--image <sha256>] [--discovery disabled|repository] [--preview|--apply] [--json] [--lang en|tr]
Preview or add a validated reusable coding template through governed configuration; existing kind bindings are preserved. On a terminal the missing choices are asked and a preview card is confirmed; elsewhere a missing choice lists the admitted values. Without --image the configured worker image is used; when no admitted CLI runs there, the error names the admitted images. Without --discovery the template keeps the discovery mode of the admitted profiles it derives from; --discovery disabled hides repository instructions from the worker.

cli.init.registry.help:
deckent init registry --scope <id> --provider <id> --kind <kind> --pool <id> --execution-slots <n> --in-flight-slots <n> [--discovery disabled|repository] --preview|--apply [--json] [--lang en|tr]
Requires execution.docker configuration. Detects the selected native CLI version in the configured Docker image; never overwrites an authored registry. Without --discovery the worker runs with repository instructions hidden (disabled); a CLI without a verified way to hide them needs --discovery repository.
cli.audit.summary: Verify audit history and checkpoint evidence
cli.audit.rebaseline.summary: Accept a reviewed audit drift as the new baseline
cli.audit.help:
Usage: deckent audit [<action>]
  (no action) | verify [--scope <id>] [--checkpoint <file|->] [--export-checkpoint [<file>]] [--json]
    read-only; shows the last checkpoint and what the check cannot do; exit 1 unless the result is match
    --export-checkpoint <file> writes the latest checkpoint there (0600, never over an existing file); without a file it prints JSON
  rebaseline --scope <id> --reason <text>
    after a governed review, accept a policy/producer drift or a possible wipe as the new baseline; a card on a person's terminal only (refused for AI); audited with the reason
This catches a change made from the same account; it does not prevent one. Keep exported checkpoints off this machine.
cli.help.top.surfaces:
Surfaces (one installation, one set of typed operations):
  deckent             the interactive terminal on a real terminal; this help
                      when piped
  deckent <command>   this CLI: one call, one result; text for people, --json
                      for scripts and AI agents
  deckent-mcp         MCP server: Deckent operations as tools for AI clients;
                      policy grants decide which ones they may use
mcp.help.text:
deckent-mcp: Deckent operations as MCP tools over stdio for AI clients.

Usage:
  deckent-mcp [--project <dir>]

Options:
  --project <dir>   project directory (default: the current directory)
  -h, --help        show this help

Protocol messages use stdout; start failures are written to stderr with a non-zero exit.
cli.help.top.commands: Commands (deckent <command> --help shows each action and its options):
cli.help.top.options:
Options:
  -h, --help          help; deckent <command> [<action>] --help for one command
  -v, --version       version and build
  --json              one machine-readable result on stdout; errors on stderr
  --lang en|tr        output language
  --no-color          plain text without colours
  --scope <id>        the scope a command works in (see each command)
  --full-access       open the terminal in full-access mode
cli.help.top.footer:
Without an action a command runs the read named above, acts on its own
(terminal, init, monitor, models, config, doctor, paths), or lists its actions
and names the missing argument (exit 2).
Exit codes: 0 OK, 1 error, 2 usage, 78 configuration.

cli.coding.instructions.help:
deckent coding instructions [status] [--json] [--lang en|tr]
Shows the worker instruction file of the work target (execution.workerInstructions; the project root when no work target is configured): path, size, SHA-256 and whether workers get it now.
deckent coding instructions trust|revoke [--target <id>] --scope <id> [--lang en|tr]
Trusts (or takes back) exactly the file's current content for that folder and, with a work target, for its base ref. A card on your own terminal shows the path, size, SHA-256 and first lines; AI tools, MCP, pipes and --json are refused. Decided on the config write permission for execution.workerInstructions and recorded in the audit log. A changed file is untrusted again.

cli.help.summary.recovery: Lost-worker recovery: rollout progress and your blind review
cli.help.recovery:
Usage: deckent recovery [--scope <id>] [--json]
  Read-only: per measured lost-worker rule its shadow cases since the last false alarm, and how often the recovery model agreed with your blind choices. A model's choice of a case you have not answered is never shown.
deckent recovery review [--scope <id>]
  On your terminal only: each case the model decided in shadow, without its choice. You say whether the worker really was lost and what you would have done; your answer is recorded, then the model's choice is shown. Answers measure agreement and change no work.
Standing grants and rule promotions: deckent policy recovery.

cli.uninstall.help.summary: Preview or uninstall one installation; keep data by default.
cli.uninstall.help:
deckent uninstall [--purge] [--dry-run] [--json]
--dry-run and --json only preview the exact plan. Removal requires a person in their own terminal, installation-wide policy and durable plan approval. Global data and project .deckent folders stay by default. --purge first creates and verifies a backup that deckent backup restore can bring back (its authority key is passphrase-protected), then asks for one confirmation card (Cancel by default) and deletes only the listed authority files (ledger, policy, bindings, installation identity, approval key) and the backup audit records sealed with this installation's key. Folders without such a record (runs, artifacts, signers and others) stay and are listed; an unsafe or moved authority file stops the purge before anything is deleted. If a purge is interrupted, a later run shows one card for exactly the remaining files. Shared or unknown ownership is kept and reported. Managed-install and retention policies still apply. Native service removal is supported on Linux; other platforms print manual steps. The CLI package stays for removal through its package manager.
